notes: Beat as planned: in private at the inn, Myrddin completes the Pennod 17 tale (verbatim echoes of the storm: eira, gwynt cryf, taranau, mellt, pawb yn cysgu ond Elen, curo curo curo, the blanket). Uthr, dying, had named the baby Arthur and given him to Myrddin to keep safe; Myrddin left the castle with him; when he went through the gate the king had died. He chose faithful Cynyr in Cwm Helyg; Cynyr promised to raise the child as his own and keep the secret. 'Arthur yw dy enw di.' Cynyr kneels; Arthur: 'Dad! Paid! … Ti yw fy nhad i.' Elen weeps; Mali is furious that everyone kept the secret for eleven years, then forgives; Dafi curls round Arthur's neck.

New facts, chosen to leave later chapters free: Arthur was born in the castle at Caerllion, in winter, with grey eyes; Uthr had been ill a long time and the lords were already fighting; nobody knew of the son. The queen's fate is left open. Cynyr's joke closes the secrets: 'mae'r ddraig yn fy nghegin i, wrth gwrs.' Modlen brings cawl: 'cawl i'r brenin, felly. Ond does dim pasteiod!'

Arthur does not want the crown at the end ('Dw i ddim eisiau'r dynged hon … Dw i eisiau mynd yn ôl i Gwm Helyg'); Myrddin: the council will wait for his answer tomorrow. This hands 31 its beat. From 30 the narrator calls him Arthur; the family still say 'Arth' in moments of habit (Mali).

Pluperfect roedd … wedi appears 14×, with the plan's contrast 'Pan es i drwy'r porth, roedd y brenin wedi marw.' cyn / ar ôl / wrth + verbal noun and ers + time are all demonstrated; 'cafodd … ei eni' / 'Ble ces i fy ngeni?' is glossed and receptive (cael-passive is G32); it appears only in the C8 personal prompt as a recognition model.

primary_new_grammar.label: Pluperfect roedd / ro'n i … wedi + verbal noun (Roedd y brenin wedi marw; Ro'n i wedi addo), contrasted with the preterite in pan-clauses (Pan es i drwy'r porth, roedd y brenin wedi marw); cyn, ar ôl, wrth + verbal noun (Cyn marw …; Ar ôl clywed …; Wrth gerdded …); ers + time for a state continuing to now (ers un ar ddeg o flynyddoedd, dw i'n cadw cyfrinach)

cover.alt: By the fire in the inn at night, big-bearded Cynyr kneels before the boy Arthur, who grips his hands to stop him; Elen weeps, Cai stares, Mali stands apart by the window, and Myrddin watches from a stool by the fire.
cover.art_brief: The common room of the small inn by the church in Caerllion at night, the door locked and only the family inside (warm firelight on limewashed walls and smoke-dark beams, an unglazed shuttered window with snow on the sill). Cynyr (broad, fifties, huge golden-blond beard to mid-chest, brown cloak with round silver brooch) has risen from his chair and gone down on one knee before Arthur, his big head bowed. Arthur (11, slight, untidy brown hair with cowlick, freckles, grey eyes, oversized moss-green tunic; NO crown), just up from the bench, grips his foster-father's hands to stop him, face distressed. The shining sword from the stone leans against the wall by the fire. Elen (tall, dark hair streaked grey under a white linen veil, green dress, keys at her belt) weeps in her chair by the fire, smiling through tears; Cai (15, ginger-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak) stands astonished; Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, oatmeal-grey cloak with a curl of smoke from it) stands apart by the window, arms folded, red-faced. Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, patched deep-blue robe, round wire spectacles catching the firelight) sits on a stool by the fire, bareheaded, his tall black brimmed hat on his knees. No text.

grammar.rule_cy: roedd / ro'n i … wedi + berfenw = cyn amser arall yn y gorffennol. Pan es i …, roedd e wedi marw. · cyn, ar ôl, wrth + berfenw. · ers + amser = o amser yn y gorffennol (gyda mae / dw i: hyd heddiw).

grammar.nodyn_en: Roedd … wedi = 'had done': one past event before another (Pan es i drwy'r porth, roedd y brenin wedi marw). Cyn, ar ôl and wrth take a verb-noun: cyn marw 'before dying', ar ôl clywed 'after hearing', wrth gerdded 'while walking'. Ers + time with the present = 'for … (and still)'.
